candidate: Defend does not reduce direct Spirit Power Damage to Dahan
reason: The source defines Defend by both recipient and damage source: Invaders dealing Damage to the land/Dahan. The existing bank tests how Defend stacks, applies to both recipients, persists, and affects Ravage counterattack, but never tests whether it prevents explicitly harmful Spirit Power Damage. Assuming that all Damage in a Defended land is reduced would pass those existing prompts and fail this one. That isolates a distinct source-defined eligibility boundary; the Ravage comparison is a control, not the source of novelty.
recommended_question: A land has Defend 3. An ordinary Spirit Power directly and explicitly deals 2 Damage to Dahan there; it does not cause a Ravage, and the Spirit has no special rule altering that Damage. Does Defend reduce it? Compare with Invaders dealing 2 Ravage Damage to the land and Dahan in that same Defended land.
predetermined_answer: Defend does not reduce the direct Spirit Power Damage: 2 Damage is still dealt to the Dahan as instructed. Defend only reduces Damage dealt by Invaders to the land/Dahan. For the 2-Damage Invader Ravage, subtract Defend 3 from each recipient total down to a minimum of zero, so both land and Dahan take 0 Damage.
novelty_class: Source-defined source-of-Damage boundary / consequential exception interaction
not_mechanical_recombination: Q18 establishes that explicit Power instructions may harm Dahan but does not ask about mitigation. Q31 establishes additive Defend against Invader Damage but does not ask whether a different source is eligible for Defend. A new eligibility condition is needed to distinguish the two cases; substituting another number or recipient alone would not supply it.
